title: Crystal Gazing: Its History and Practice, with a Discussion of the Evidence for Telepathic Scrying
author: Northcote W. Thomas; introduction by Andrew Lang
edition_cited: London: Alexander Moring, The De La More Press, 1905 (Cornell scan)
tradition: British psychical research on scrying (S.P.R. circle)
locator_hints: Introduction by Andrew Lang (pp. ix-xlvii): his sitters' reports; 'milky, then black, then pictures'; who can and cannot scry
Chapter III 'Crystal Visions' (p. 22 ff.): dark-funnel experiment that 'filled with light'; ball filling with mist or vanishing; Ibn Khaldun
Chapter IV 'The Speculum, and the Method of using it' (p. 32 ff.), esp. pp. 39-41: Lang's and Thomas's practical advice, Goodrich-Freer's advice
summary: A survey of scrying by an anthropologist who says he has never seen anything himself, with a long introduction by Andrew Lang reporting what his own acquaintances saw. Lang says the usual sequence in successful first attempts was that the glass ball 'grew milky, then black; then the pictures appeared', and that some strong visualisers got the mist but never pictures. Chapter III describes a first experiment made by looking into a perfectly dark funnel with the head covered, which 'filled with light' before pictures came. Chapter IV collects practical advice: sit alone, back to the light, ball on a dark cloth, exclude reflections, gaze about five minutes (Lang) or ten minutes or until the eyes tire, in repeated sets some days apart (Thomas); Lang holds that if nothing comes in two or three trials it probably never will. Historical chapters quote older recipes (Trithemius, Hollenzwang, Egyptian ink-mirror).
why_relevant: Gives concrete beginner procedure and the standard onset signs (clouding, darkening, the speculum vanishing) for light and imagery seen in the open-eye field, with explicit statements about who fails.

date_evidence.basis: title page of the scanned edition reads 1905; archive.org metadata date 1905

notes: Thomas and Lang are both non-scryers reporting others; first-person scryer testimony is in the Goodrich-Freer record. OCR is fair; some garbling.
